summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of mast cell degranulation syndrome was admitted for an acute exacerbation triggered by psychological stress, presenting with pleuritic chest pain, shortness of breath, epigastric pain, nausea, and generalized pruritus. She was treated with her established inpatient regimen of intravenous Dilaudid, Ativan, and Benadryl, administered via infusion over time, with close observation confirming safety and efficacy without need for IV push dosing. Diagnostic workup included a normal EKG, negative cardiac enzymes, and a chest X-ray showing clear lungs but a new posterior density recommended for outpatient CT evaluation. Laboratory results showed mild leukocytopenia, deemed non-acute. Her symptoms resolved to baseline, vital signs remained stable, and she was discharged home on her prior medications with follow-up arranged with her primary care provider and allergist.
